verdict.rationale: Anytype's own docs describe self-hosting its sync and backup network from a team-maintained Docker image, and the app itself runs local-first, with a CLI that runs it as a headless server. The documented limitation is that switching to a self-hosted network means exporting your channels and importing them into a new identity. Setup depth is thin and there is no hands-on corroboration. missing for 10: in-depth self-host setup documentation (network configuration, requirements, operations), independent or hands-on reports of successful self-hosting, and a seamless move to self-hosting without re-creating your identity.
